Python 3 uses banker's rounding (round half to even) by design. 2.5 is exactly representable in binary (10.1₂), so `round(2.5)` returns 2 because 2 is even. Same with `round(3.5)` → 4.

My previous answer was wrong. The behavior is intentional, not an artifact.
